plan.mechanism:
ONE allocator: the RightColumn flex-col is the sole height authority, every panel sizes to its CONTENT by default, an explicit yield order decides who scrolls when the viewport is short, and a single structural spacer (NOT a content panel) absorbs all positive slack. Concretely:

(1) DEFAULT = content-sized for everything. Squad Orders stays `auto` (flex:0 0 auto, content height, never scrolls — owner's hard requirement). Task Org becomes `auto` too (the squad list is 5 rows + hint ≈ 257px of content; it should show fully, never be the crushed sink). Logistics becomes `auto` (8 supply bars + CERP footer ≈ 282px; its hardcoded 182 is DELETED so the bars never clip). Village (now a DockPanel, see changes) is `auto`. No panel is `grow` anymore — the elastic role is removed from every content panel, which kills both the crushed-Task-Org pathology AND the all-collapsed void at their shared root (single-grow-sink).

(2) SINK = one structural spacer. Add `<div className="flex-1 min-h-0" aria-hidden />` as the LAST child of the RightColumn flex-col (below Logistics). It is the ONLY flex:1 element in the column, so it owns 100% of positive slack regardless of which panels are collapsed/short. When everything is collapsed it fills the void (state 09); when a content panel is short (states 01/05) the slack lands in the spacer as neutral column background, not inside a half-empty panel. This decouples "who never scrolls" (Squad Orders) from "who absorbs slack" (the spacer) — that decoupling is the whole fix for the void class (07/09) and the internal dead-space class (01/05).

(3) FIT = explicit yield order when content > colH (state 10). When the column would overflow, the LEAST-critical panel yields first via internal scroll, in this priority: Logistics → Task Org → (Squad Orders protected, never scrolls). Implement by giving Logistics and Task Org a `maxHeight` tied to remaining budget so they cap-and-scroll internally instead of pushing the column past colH; Squad Orders has no cap. If even the protected floor overflows (a viewport shorter than Squad Orders itself), the COLUMN gets `overflow-y-auto` as the final graceful fallback (whole column scrolls, last child never clipped silently). Since the spacer is flex:1 min-h-0 it contributes 0 under pressure, so it never competes with real content for the scarce space.

Net behaviour across all 10 states: Squad Orders always full + never scrolls; squad list (Task Org) shows all rows compactly; Logistics shows all 8 bars; collapsing any panel just hands its space to the spacer (no void); short viewport degrades by scrolling Logistics first, then Task Org, then the whole column — never Squad Orders. The trichotomy collapses to: every panel `auto` (content height, optional max-cap) + one spacer sink + column-scroll fallback. The fixed/grow magic numbers (182, minHeight 64, max-clamp 560) all disappear into this one model.

changes.what: Add a single always-present structural spacer as the LAST child of the RightColumn flex-col: `<div className="flex-1 min-h-0" aria-hidden />` placed after the Logistics DockPanel. This is the column's sole flex:1 sink, owning all positive slack. (Optionally render a faint centered 'panels collapsed — click a header to expand' hint inside it only when all panels are collapsed.)
changes.why: Decouples slack-absorption from any content panel. Directly fixes the all-collapsed void (state 09, 681px dead), the Task-Org-collapsed void (state 07, 64px), and the internal dead-space-below-short-content (states 01 ~470px, 05 ~97px). No per-state branching — one element handles every void case.

changes.what: Change Logistics from `defaultHeight={182} last` to `auto` (content height). Remove the hardcoded 182 and the `last` flag. Its body (8 SUPPLY_ROWS + inbound line + 2 CERP footer lines ≈ 282px) then renders fully and never clips by default.
changes.why: Logistics clips its supply bars (scrollH 282 vs clientH 153, scrolls:true) in EVERY open state — 01,02,03,04,05,10. The fixed 182 < required 282 is content-independent and was tuned for one state. `last` also suppressed its ResizeHandle, removing the only manual escape. Auto sizing makes 'med kits/water/food/CERP' visible everywhere.

changes.what: Change Task Organization from `grow` to `auto` (content height). Remove the grow branch reliance for this panel. The 5-row squad list + hint (~257px) now renders fully without being the crushed elastic sink.
changes.why: Task Org is crushed to a scrolling 35-92px sliver whenever a squad is selected (states 02/03/04/10: clientH 35-103 vs scrollH 257, scrolls:true) because it was the lone grow sink absorbing all of Squad Orders' expansion. Owner requires 'squad list stays compact and fully visible'. Auto sizing + the spacer (not Task Org) absorbing slack fixes this.

changes.what:
Route the village through the SAME DockPanel primitive: replace the bare `
` with `}>`. Move the village name lookup up so the title is available (or keep VillagePanel computing it and expose name).
changes.why: Village is currently a non-dock div: no collapse chevron, no resize, no participation in the layout (state 05). It gives the column two different header grammars and no way to collapse the village to reach Logistics (✕ only deselects). Routing through DockPanel gives it the collapse chevron, a layout id (togglePanel works), and the unified auto/spacer behaviour — and removes the jarring two-panel→one-panel structural jump.

changes.what: Strip VillagePanel's root wrapper from `<div className="border-b border-line p-2 flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto">` down to `<div className="p-2">`, and remove its hand-rolled title row's reliance on owning the header (the ✕ moves to the DockPanel right slot; keep ✕ = deselect). DockPanel now owns flex/scroll/border.
changes.why: Eliminates the double-wrapped flex-1/min-h-0/overflow-y-auto/border-b (RightColumn wrapper + VillagePanel root both had it) — dead inert inner flex, doubled hairline border, nested-scroll trap. One owner (DockPanel) for scroll+border. The flex-1-over-grow that produced the ~97px dead band below village content also goes away once the body is auto-sized and the spacer takes slack.

changes.what: Add a content-aware max-height + scroll fallback to the non-protected panels. Give Logistics and Task Org a `maxHeight` derived from remaining column budget (or, simplest robust version: add `overflow-y-auto` to the column wrapper itself — `className="...flex flex-col min-h-0 overflow-y-auto"` — so when total content > colH the WHOLE column scrolls instead of clipping the last child). Squad Orders gets NO cap (protected).
changes.why: Short viewport overflows by 65px and clips Logistics with no scrollbar (state 10: colH 672, panelsSum 737, overflowsColumn:true). The column had no overflow handling. Column-level scroll is the graceful final fallback that yields the least-critical content first and NEVER clips Squad Orders silently. Implements the explicit yield order: Logistics/Task Org scroll before the column does, Squad Orders last.

changes.what: Split the DockPanel `right` slot into an always-shown lightweight `badge` and a `!collapsed`-only `actions` slot. Move the header render so `actions` is gated by the existing `!collapsed` guard while `badge` stays. For Logistics: badge = LogiBadge (⚠), actions = ResupplyButtons (Convoy/Air). Also suppress the DeployBadge `—` em-dash placeholder when collapsed.
changes.where: components/screens/DeployScreen.tsx:DockPanel (header right-slot render, line ~177) + RightColumn logistics right prop + DeployBadge
changes.why: Collapsed Logistics header renders CONVOY/AIR which overflow the 344px column (AIR clipped at edge in states 06/09) and lets the user act on a hidden panel. Em-dash on collapsed Squad Orders is noise; Task Org shows nothing — three inconsistent right-edge treatments break the collapsed-stack rhythm. One guard in DockPanel fixes the overflow + the rhythm for every panel at once.

changes.what: Remove the now-dead special-case branches in DockPanel: the `grow` style branch (`flex:1 1 0%, minHeight:64`) and the `last` handling. Keep `collapsed` (28px header) and `auto` (flex:0 0 auto, content). Keep fixed/resizable branch ONLY if any panel still needs manual resize; otherwise delete it and the ResizeHandle/setPanelHeight/heights-persistence path along with the 560 clamp. Make DockPanel ignore any persisted heights[id] for auto panels.
changes.why: Once every panel is auto + spacer-sink, grow/last/fixed are unused special cases (Law: delete special cases, unify). minHeight:64 produced a 35px sub-row stub (state 10). The 560 resize clamp is column-unaware and can force overflow. Stale persisted heights for a now-non-resizable panel become un-resettable poison — ignoring heights[] for auto panels eliminates that class. (If owner wants resize kept, retain ONE resizable panel with a column-relative clamp instead of 560.)

changes.what: Add a redundant non-color collapsed cue to the DockPanel header: apply a subtle inset/darker background (e.g. `bg-panel2`) or a hairline accent to the header div when `collapsed`, in addition to the existing chevron rotation.
changes.why: Collapse state is encoded only in a ~9px chevron rotation; in state 09 three collapsed headers look nearly identical to expanded-with-empty-body. A surface cue makes collapsed rows obviously closed at milspec scale. Low cost, preserves density. (Lowest priority — purely additive polish once the structural fixes land.)
